evals.prompt: I need to add a new achievement to our game: a hidden standard achievement worth 10 points called 'First Victory' for winning the first match. Show me the JSON and the GPC commands, and how to preview before it goes live.
evals.expected_output: Provides achievement JSON and creates it with gpc games achievements create --file, using --dry-run first
expectations: Shows an achievement.json with achievementType STANDARD and initialState HIDDEN
Uses gpc games achievements create --file achievement.json --dry-run before applying
Mentions setting the game id via --game-id, GPC_GAME_ID, or games.applicationId
Notes the id is the numeric Play Games application id, not the package name

evals.prompt: We keep our leaderboard definitions as JSON files in the repo. In CI I want to detect when the live Play Games config has drifted from our files before we push changes. How do I do that with GPC?
evals.expected_output: Shows gpc games leaderboards diff against the file, then update to apply
expectations: Shows gpc games leaderboards diff <leaderboard-id> --file leaderboard.json
Explains diff reports field-by-field differences between local and remote
Recommends diff in CI to detect drift, then update --file to apply
Shows gpc games leaderboards update <leaderboard-id> --file leaderboard.json

evals.prompt: How do I list all the achievements configured for our game as JSON for a dashboard, and where do I get the game id from?
evals.expected_output: Shows gpc games achievements list --json and how to resolve the numeric game id
expectations: Explains the JSON envelope has the items key plus nextPageToken and meta.count
Explains the numeric game application id comes from Play Games Services > Configuration
